hypotheses.basis: The word 'must' creates a deontic prohibition on performing the action unless the prerequisite event has occurred. The behavioral rule is: updating a booking is forbidden when the user id has not been obtained.
unresolved_terms: temporal ordering (before/first) not expressible in propositional atom logic

hypotheses.basis: The policy imposes a positive obligation on the agent to obtain the user id as a prerequisite step. The behavioral rule is: the agent is required to perform the obtaining event; the prohibition on updating is derivative of this obligation.
unresolved_terms: whether the obligation to obtain exists independently of any intended update action

hypotheses.basis: The 'must' creates a standalone obligation on the agent to obtain the user id, where the violation is the failure to obtain itself, independent of whether updating occurs. 'Before updating a booking' is read as the contextual motivation for the obligation rather than a condition that gates the violation. This differs from existing readings where the violation is tied to the act of updating.

hypotheses.basis: The 'must first obtain…before updating' is read as a factual capability constraint rather than a deontic prohibition: updating is impossible without first obtaining, so no violation clause is needed because the prohibited state cannot arise. The behavioral difference from existing readings is that there is no obligation or prohibition to enforce—only an inherent precondition. The agent is not 'forbidden' from updating without obtaining; rather, the action simply cannot be performed.
